Topic: Fast live magic browse · inspection only
DM procedure: A player asking to see magic items requests a few actionable local sale/commission/service options, NOT an automatic purchase, rare-stock audit or comprehensive research pass. First reuse verified current-scene PLAY_NOW offers or the settlement's already prepared Dealers/Stock/Events and present 2–5 real options with known price, succinct mechanics and usefulness; no reroll, web search or record writes just to display known stock. For a first unprepared town, use the established single genuine Rural market d100 and eligible R01–R30 Templates draw, preferring previously source-verified item entries; retain the result in an unsynced in-conversation ledger until natural batch sync. Broad 5etools/Griffon source research applies to candidate-pool maintenance and specific genuinely unknown selected items, not every live browse; at most one narrow lookup for an unknown material mechanic, no blanket 12-site searches. Distinguish ready purchase from a working heirloom NOT FOR SALE or referral. A browse does not authorize purchase/hold, trigger estate/Blackthorn/tax validation or require a committed checkpoint before presenting options; preserve stable draws and exact offers for later sync.

Start with the live README and confirmed checkpoint. Identify the settlement by canonical name, region and known aliases. On confirmed approach, inquiry or return, search Dealers, Stock and Events by settlement and trade, including earlier first-preparation events with zero contacts. If prepared, resume that market, settle commitments, then resolve due reviews. For a new market use City, Market town or Village below. Templates supplies reusable designs. Dealers owns people and review dates, Stock owns physical lots and terms, Events owns preparation draws, transactions and review history. Reveal only what V learns through play.

Use the Political Reference, map and confirmed local lore as relevant. Identify the livelihood, who pays for it, where the item came from, who owns it and why they might part with it. Use regional trade routes and travel times for outside suppliers. Ordinary goods and services support the shop. Repeat magical staples require credible repeat demand and supply.

Build outward by district and trade as the party explores. Spread distinct, attainable choices across independent businesses, guild contacts, estate sales and makers. A counter usually has zero or one noteworthy piece. Include immediately affordable offers, more expensive secondhand goods and commissions where the local economy supports them. Orsaven is an example, not a required inventory. For a new eligible city use Unassigned city activation once. For any other new city, including after those packages are used, prepare its first relevant district from local trades and Source breadth. Expand an existing city only when a distinct district, supplier or inquiry supports it. Verify access and name collisions before recording a new owner.

Start with a local industry and its actual customers. Adapt one or more Templates to different local owners. For a broad inquiry, prepare a few distinct purchase paths where credible, such as a used tool for sale, a conditional sale and a traveling maker. Give an outside lead a destination and plausible timing. For a new local market, use Rural market rolls and the R01–R30 pool in Templates.

Start with a household, workshop, shrine, steward or visiting trader. One working heirloom, surplus item, visiting seller or referral may be all the settlement supports. If nothing is available locally, identify who might know a seller and where the party could reach them, when the fiction supports it. For a new local market, use Rural market rolls and the R01–R30 pool in Templates.

Dealers records the settlement, ordinary trade and introduction status. Stock records each actual object under its settlement and dealer, plus quantity, source, owner or consignor, effect and terms. Establish how V could discover it. State an asking price for an outright sale, a concrete condition for a negotiated sale, or who could make another. Preserve genuinely private heirlooms. Record mere referrals in Dealers.

Consider local demand first, then the current party’s gear, skills and interests. Across a settlement vary effects, prices and acquisition routes. Include useful inexpensive options as well as distinctive pieces where feasible. V design references and Restock candidates guide research only. An old quote or favorite item creates no current offer or order.

For candidate-pool preparation, planned shop refreshes and narrow verification of a genuinely new selected item, use the 5etools GitHub repository https://github.com/5etools-mirror-3/5etools-src/ and the interactive catalogue https://5e.tools/items.html as two views of the same catalogue. Search the repository directly via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/5etools-mirror-3/5etools-src/main/data/items.json and consult related item and variant data for entries defined elsewhere in the repository. Search The Griffon’s Saddlebag Book One https://drive.google.com/file/d/1mrYLP0lz0eRmNqDFQL4ijHsgeoc4H-io/view and Book Two https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xNn1fO0qx4jdZU71rBqNvdoMNLKXEPFy/view alongside it. Cite the underlying book, edition and page or entry for each selected item. Match the source code to the campaign edition (DMG for 2014, XDMG for 2024).

Use third-party books for inspiration or verified entries. Record publisher and page/entry; check activation, duration, charges, attunement, recharge and practical power. Campaign bans apply, including healing potions.

On a broad inquiry, give several actionable options at the settlement’s scale. Name the trade or contact, effect, approximate cost or condition and how to follow up. Show a tool in use when visiting its owner. Distinguish a ready seller, a conditional seller, a commission and an unconfirmed lead. Record only discoveries actually played.

Use existing agreed quotes. For new terms use condition, local demand and the owner’s motive; guides are 5–50 gp for minor utility, 150–500 gp for uncommon and 2,000–5,000 gp for rare. Brokers need a seller and credible buyer with means. Establish authority, commission fee, minimum, custody, expiry and payment terms as applicable.

A willing seller accepts the asking price without a roll. Let V ask what matters, propose a price, trade, replacement or payment schedule, and decide whether to accept. Set the owner’s authority, limits, DC and possible concessions before any uncertain check. V controls V’s Persuasion roll unless delegated. Success earns a real concession; on a miss the standing offer normally survives. A materially different proposal can reopen talks. Record only actual offers, commitments and payments from play.

Record the actual effect requested, stated budget, maker, material, fee or deposit, lead time and delivery condition when known. Distinguish a referral from a maker’s firm quote. Use the same inquiry record when it becomes an order. Only agreed terms reserve an item. State quantity, holder and expiry. V chooses whether to commit.

Resolve dated commitments first, then overdue owner and business reviews through confirmed game time, even if V never met the owner. Preserve standing terms while an offer is available. On return, show what a local contact could know about a change and where a moved object or successor might be found. Share only what V learns.

Events owns confirmed inquiries, quotes, holds, orders, sales and deliveries. Use one source event ID and separate posting-leg IDs under README Shared run protocol. Scheduled Markets writes market records only and hands missing personal/shared/history legs to live sync or Record Maintenance; estate legs go to Estate Ledger Updates. Live sync may complete all evidenced legs of a played transaction; Maintenance repairs party/shared/history legs without simulating trade. Check existing receipts before every leg and acknowledge verified completion. Independent NPC trade never posts V money or gear. Preserve player decisions and campaign time.
Keep the Day 216 browse in Events and the historical quotes in Restock candidates. The old Day 223 deliveries and Day 230 bulk refresh are superseded. Current terms live in Stock.

Topic: Closed sessions and retired source notes
DM procedure: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xxrGQJ1kWeL7tffEb6J-fgjaK-3IYE2PpQJeHS_F4Lw/edit
https://docs.google.com/document/d/12cdmQAxepOHUdMwWK_o4wJMTFBna8A2MYrtoXmSN1cM/edit?tab=t.2gercvxhabnl

On preparing a settlement, anchor reviews to a confirmed local market date, even for undiscovered contacts. Record Next due and a specific question in Dealers. Defaults in campaign days: 14–28 for an open sale or consignment, 28–56 for working property, heirlooms or a stable business. Stagger reviews. A deadline, route departure, closure or played event takes precedence. A pass or silence leaves an offer available to other buyers; it is not a penalty. A question alone grants no hold. Preserve agreed holds, prices and commission terms through their stated dates.

Apply established events and commitments first. For uncertain outcomes use the percentile procedure below. Each due review has one primary subject and one next day. If a shop also has an independently dated business event, give it its own event ID. Do not roll a fresh business hazard at each item review. Execute fresh RNG for play; a test seed or example never resolves a campaign event. Check verified local causes first. Trace the affected item, buyer or supplier, route, dated source event and when this owner learns of it. Apply a known physical effect once. Roll only for remaining uncertainty. For recovery identify an available supplier, route and earliest plausible delivery before offering replacement stock. Follow README Shared run protocol before adjudication: check already-due causal prerequisites, acquire the cooperative writer lease, and persist/verify each draw stage. An unresolved prerequisite holds only its dependent event.

A motivated owner may sell, withdraw, change terms, consign elsewhere, travel, pass an heirloom down or replace a tool. A workshop may move, gain a partner or apprentice, pass to a successor, change trade or close. For moves and succession track the object, former and new custodian, location and any outstanding agreement. Only introduce replacement stock with its own source and terms. Nearby businesses and credible referrals can offer new choices when an old lead ends.

Use a stable review/event ID based on settlement, contact and due day. In Events record elapsed day, cause, any roll, outcome (including no change), and next review. Update Dealers last review and Next due; update Stock only when availability, custody, quantity or terms change. Leave a trail for sold, withdrawn or relocated items so the same unique piece cannot be offered twice. Preparation and private changes do not count as player discovery. Use README PREPARED/DRAW_STARTED/RESOLVED recovery stages in the same Events record before dependent postings. Recover an interrupted draw from its saved result or original tool evidence; otherwise mark DRAW_UNRESOLVED and do not reroll. Consumer ACKs close only the corresponding verified handoff.

Before rolling, classify the due question. Open offer or consignment 35%; working tool or conditional sale 10%; family heirloom or prized possession 5%; proprietor, premises or staffing 5%; fresh consignment at an empty contact with an identified supplier 15%. Roll d100 once: at or below the chance triggers one development, otherwise record no change. These are chances of any eligible development per review, not chances of sale. Keep the existing 14–28 or 28–56 day schedules; use the supplier’s established date for incoming goods.

For an open offer add 20 percentage points for a concrete, funded buyer or an impending consignment deadline with uncertain outcome; subtract 15 for a documented obstacle such as poor fit or inaccessible transport. Apply at most one net modifier, decided before rolling. For a working tool, heirloom or business, double the base chance only with a specific pressure such as retirement, a new contract or an impending move. A proven outcome happens directly. With no plausible outcome, record no change. Player silence has no modifier.

Before rolling, list plausible outcomes and cross out impossible ones. Open offer: sale 5, withdrawal 2, move to another seller 2, revised terms 1. Tool or heirloom: transfer or loan to a known custodian 3, travel with owner 3, change in sale terms 2, replace or retire the piece 2. Business: proprietor or staffing change 5, relocation 3, closure or change of trade 2. Incoming goods: choose verified offers from actual suppliers. On a triggered development, if multiple outcomes remain, roll uniformly from 1 to their total weight and use cumulative weights in the listed order. One eligible outcome resolves directly. A sale needs a buyer with means; a replacement needs an identifiable new piece. Respect holds, custody and existing promises.

For k missed review dates with identical odds, pressure and eligible outcomes, use one cumulative probability 1−(1−p)^k (p as a fraction). Use an executed uniform random fraction against that threshold. If triggered, sample the first successful review j=1…k with weights (1−p)^(j−1)p, then resolve as of that day and reassess later due events from the resulting state. Batch only established dates; when conditions or commitments change, split there. In Events record dates covered, subject, odds and reason, actual draws, outcome, custody and next due. A recorded event or covered interval is never rolled twice.

ADMIN-SHOP7-20261119-001: Caereth (Crownsunder; user's Caerenth), Veyrhold (Veyran Commonwealth), Ilarath (Ilvaran), Allhaven (explicitly selected by player), plus UNASSIGNED-CITY-01/02/03. Templates indexes them; Dealers and Stock own details. Named additions anchored to confirmed Day228; first job checks may precede routine turnover. No visited/discovered state inferred.

UNASSIGNED-CITY-01/02/03 are one-use DM preparation packages, not settlements or active stock. Zero units and blank opening/review dates are deliberate. At actual preparation of one of the next three distinct large unnamed cities without an established market, bind one unused package to that city, check canon/trade/name collisions and existing contacts, adapt only unrevealed incompatible details, then set prepared quantities and dates from the confirmed local date A. Change all matching Dealers/Stock settlement keys and mark the binding in Templates plus one Events ID ACTIVATE-M7-UCnn-<city>-D<day>, preserving M7 lot IDs. Never activate the same package twice, clone stock, or bind to Caereth/Veyrhold/Ilarath/Allhaven/another existing market. Assignment is not player discovery.

For unassigned rows, Dealers review text gives A+offset; convert it to a numeric campaign day on binding. No retrospective turnover before A. Named opening Day228 is preparation as-of, not a played visit. Fixed job targets in Dealers are checked even without V; asking does not reset a worker's job to start anew. Resolve actual completion/custody first, then set the resulting open-offer review 14–28 days later or next relevant obstacle date. Apply existing percentile/recovery rules only to genuine uncertainty and confirmed elapsed time.

A maker contact is a limited commission path in Dealers, not finished Stock. Prepared price/deposit/duration becomes an offered quote only when introduced and current bench/material supply is checked. Lead time begins only after an accepted order; deposits, delivery and acceptance require played evidence and separate idempotent Events. One concurrent enchanted order per listed maker. Confirm actual completion before any delivery; ordinary work, finite magical reserves and material access limit production.

M7 rows use the full source pool under Source breadth; each lot identifies its book and entry; summaries are reminders, exact cited entry and RULES govern. Opening charged pieces are explicitly full unless otherwise stated; finite-use items retain their recorded remaining quantities. Record subsequent demonstrations/usage. No healing potions, food/water loophole industry, 2024 replacements or automatic enchantment transfer to V's sword. Ordinary NPC magical work remains limited by Political Reference; PC item mechanics remain as approved.

For a broad city inquiry, present a useful spread of currently reachable ready-sale, conditional and commission leads, with prices/effects, not every private row as known. Buying at a ready asking price requires no Persuasion roll. Identify the actual owner/consignor by the stable dealer-and-lot role; personal names can be added once collision-checked on introduction. Role-based ownership is not an unknown sale authority. Existing held/sold lots, agreed prices, previous contacts and player-controlled spending always survive later preparation.

Topic: Source breadth • every settlement and future review
DM procedure: Search across both Griffon’s Saddlebag books and the full 5etools item catalogue using the GitHub data linked under Primary sources, including supplements, settings and adventures. Begin with the trade, buyer and effects sought. Compare candidates from several books, including books absent from nearby markets; vary combat roles, exploration, social uses, working tools, consumables, rarity and price. Existing stock and example lists are starting points only. Verify the named item, book and edition before use. Use the approved 2014-compatible entry where available; flag a revised-only mechanic for a player ruling before introducing it. Respect explicit bans, unique-item custody and setting-specific prerequisites. Record source and entry/page alongside each selection. Use this procedure for new contacts, commissions and genuine replacement opportunities.

Reuse known owners, local facts and commitments first. On first preparation for an ordinary town, village or hold, roll d100 once for its total number of local magical contacts. Town: 01–20 one, 21–75 two, 76–100 three. Village or small hold: 01–25 none, 26–85 one, 86–100 two. Count existing relevant contacts toward that total and always keep them. For a broad inquiry with zero contacts, give an actionable outside lead if a known route and supplier support one. A settled market keeps its first result on every visit.

Filter by settlement size, livelihood, terrain, actual access and owner means. Rows marked Town / village fit either scale. Include any later compatible R-numbered rows in the draw. To extend the pool, append the next unused R number with scale, trade, local fit/access, sourced item, ownership and terms. Retain existing IDs so old rolls stay readable. A visiting seller needs a credible arrival and departure. For the first slot prefer eligible SALE or CONDITION rows when any fit; subsequent slots may include services and referrals. For an exact-item request use any established matching owner, or a credible maker/referral if none stocks it. Sort eligible IDs ascending, roll uniformly 1…N and select that position. Remove the selected owner and item for this settlement before the next draw. A single eligible row resolves directly; an empty pool produces no invented stock. These are models for distinct local pieces. Never copy a unique item or an existing consignment.

Use one stable first-preparation event per settlement, including a zero-contact result. Record cutoff, scale, eligible template IDs, actual draws and selection under the shared draw protocol. Bind each selected row to a distinct local owner and lot; record referrals in Dealers only. On return use Return visits and independent trade, Review dates and engagement, and the shared turnover and posting rules. For a triggered incoming consignment, select only from the identified supplier’s eligible designs, with a traceable piece, route and earliest actual availability. Existing holders, agreements and prior results carry forward.
